raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46572.

With Inkling, prefill runs under the full CUDA graph by default. The fused attention-prologue extend kernel stores K/V for every token in its launch grid, which under graph replay is the padded bucket. Padding tokens (`t >= cu[B]`) get `out_cache_loc = 0` from the prefill graph buffer registry and carry stale, sometimes non-finite, rows, so they are written into KV slot 0. Sliding-window attention can later read slot 0 (KV page size below 128, the default on H200 with FA4), which turns the logits row into NaN: `torch.multinomial` asserts with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_GUMBEL_SAMPLE=0`, and with the default sampler affected requests silently return token 0 with NaN logprobs. Details and a standalone reproducer are in #46572.

## Modifications

- `inkling_attn_prologue_fused.cuh`: add the real sequence count `B` to `AttnPrologueExtendParams` and skip the KV store in `inkling_attn_prologue_extend_kernel` for tokens at or beyond `cu[B]`. Real tokens are stored exactly as before; the `out` / `k_out` / `v_out` writes for padding rows (the graph's own scratch outputs) are unchanged. `B` is already computed in the launcher (`cache_indices.size(0)`), and `cu` has `B + 1` entries.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_inkling_attn_prologue_extend_pad.py`: new kernel unit test. It fills the padded tail of `qkvr` with NaN, maps padding tokens to slot 0 as the graph runner does, and checks that slot 0 and every other unused slot stay untouched while real tokens are stored bit-identically to the kernel's own `k_out` / `v_out` and are finite (`num_pad` 1 and 8).

## Accuracy Tests

Regression test on 1x H200 (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-cu130` environment, this branch's source on `PYTHONPATH`):

| Source | Result |
|---|---|
| this commit with the `.cuh` reverted to its parent | 2 of 2 fail: `AssertionError: padded token K was stored into slot 0` |
| this commit | 2 of 2 pass |

End-to-end with the reproducer from #46572 (Inkling-NVFP4 `test` revision, 1x H200, v0.5.22, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_GUMBEL_SAMPLE=0`): unpatched, the server dies at request 14 (2 of 2 runs); with this change, all 70 requests (5 rounds) pass and the server stays up (1 run). With the default sampler unpatched, 1065 of 2000 sampled-token logprobs are NaN at the same request.

The change only skips stores for padding tokens, which no real request should read, so model outputs for real tokens are unaffected; no separate accuracy benchmark was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The change adds one read of `cu[B]` and one comparison per thread on the store path of the extend prologue, and removes the stores for padding tokens.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (See above; not benchmarked.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

detail.title: [Fix] inkling: Skip KV stores for CUDA-graph padding tokens in the fused attn prologue

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+"""The fused attn prologue extend kernel must not store K/V for the padded tail
+of a CUDA-graph launch (tokens at or beyond cu[B]); real tokens are still stored.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.inkling_attn_prologue import (
+    inkling_attn_prologue_extend,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=40, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+HEAD = 128
+W = 4
+EPS = 1e-6
+DQ = 1024
+DKV = 256
+SENTINEL = 7.0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_pad", [1, 8])
+def test_extend_prologue_skips_padded_tokens(num_pad):
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    dev = "cuda"
+    bf16 = torch.bfloat16
+    seq_lens = [5, 3]
+    num_seqs = len(seq_lens)
+    real = sum(seq_lens)
+    t = real + num_pad
+    row = DQ + 2 * DKV + 64
+
+    qkvr = torch.randn(t, row, device=dev, dtype=bf16)
+    qkvr[real:] = float("nan")  # stale non-finite rows of the padded bucket
+    k_cache = torch.randn(64, W - 1, DKV, device=dev, dtype=bf16)
+    v_cache = torch.randn(64, W - 1, DKV, device=dev, dtype=bf16)
+    cache_indices = torch.tensor([3, 4], device=dev, dtype=torch.int32)
+    cache_mask = torch.ones(num_seqs, device=dev, dtype=torch.bool)
+    has_initial_state = torch.ones(num_seqs, device=dev, dtype=torch.bool)
+    cu = torch.tensor([0, 5, real], device=dev, dtype=torch.int64)
+    # Padding tokens are attributed to the last sequence, as the production launch does.
+    si = torch.tensor(
+        [0] * seq_lens[0] + [1] * (seq_lens[1] + num_pad), device=dev, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    k_weight = torch.randn(DKV, W, device=dev, dtype=bf16) * 0.3
+    v_weight = torch.randn(DKV, W, device=dev, dtype=bf16) * 0.3
+    q_gamma = torch.randn(HEAD, device=dev, dtype=bf16)
+    k_gamma = torch.randn(HEAD, device=dev, dtype=bf16)
+
+    slots = 64
+    real_slots = torch.arange(10, 10 + real, device=dev, dtype=torch.int64)
+    loc = torch.zeros(t, device=dev, dtype=torch.int64)  # padding maps to slot 0
+    loc[:real] = real_slots
+    k_buf = torch.zeros(slots, DKV // HEAD, HEAD, device=dev, dtype=bf16)
+    v_buf = torch.zeros_like(k_buf)
+    k_buf[0] = SENTINEL
+    v_buf[0] = SENTINEL
+
+    _, k_out, v_out, _ = inkling_attn_prologue_extend(
+        qkvr=qkvr,
+        k_cache=k_cache,
+        v_cache=v_cache,
+        cache_indices=cache_indices,
+        cache_mask=cache_mask,
+        has_initial_state=has_initial_state,
+        cu=cu,
+        si=si,
+        k_weight=k_weight,
+        v_weight=v_weight,
+        track_rows=torch.empty(0, W - 1, device=dev, dtype=torch.int64),
+        track_mask=torch.empty(0, device=dev, dtype=torch.bool),
+        track_dst=torch.empty(0, device=dev, dtype=torch.int64),
+        q_gamma=q_gamma,
+        k_gamma=k_gamma,
+        eps=EPS,
+        loc=loc,
+        k_buf=k_buf,
+        v_buf=v_buf,
+        q_off=0,
+        k_off=DQ,
+        v_off=DQ + DKV,
+        dq=DQ,
+        dkv=DKV,
+        activation=None,
+        use_residual=True,
+        do_store=True,
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    untouched = torch.ones(slots, device=dev, dtype=torch.bool)
+    untouched[real_slots] = False
+    sentinel = torch.full_like(k_buf[0], SENTINEL)
+    assert torch.equal(k_buf[0], sentinel), "padded token K was stored into slot 0"
+    assert torch.equal(v_buf[0], sentinel), "padded token V was stored into slot 0"
+    assert not k_buf[untouched][1:].any(), "padded token K was stored into a slot"
+    assert not v_buf[untouched][1:].any(), "padded token V was stored into a slot"
+
+    # Real tokens are still stored, and equal to the kernel's own k/v outputs.
+    k_real = k_out[:real].reshape(real, DKV)
+    v_real = v_out[:real].reshape(real, DKV)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        k_buf[real_slots].view(real, DKV), k_real, rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        v_buf[real_slots].view(real, DKV), v_real, rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+    assert torch.isfinite(k_buf[real_slots]).all()
+    assert torch.isfinite(v_buf[real_slots]).all()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
